observations: Photo 0 shows a blue industrial extruder-type machine inside a shipping container, mounted on a steel frame with motors, hoppers, barrels, and partial plastic wrapping.
Photos 1 and 2 show multiple similar blue machines in a warehouse, some stacked on racks and some wrapped in protective plastic.
No brand, model, serial number, or nameplate is readable in any of the three photos.
A watermark reading "POSTED ON JIJI" and "MARTHA OKPALA" appears across the images.
The machines have the general form of plastic extrusion or pelletizing equipment with drive motors, heating zones, and hoppers.

claims.claim: recycle waste nylon materials into raw material
claims.evidence: Photos show an extruder-type machine but cannot confirm it processes nylon or produces usable raw material.
Plastic wrapping is visible, but there are no seals, invoices, or documentation to confirm new status.
Motor power and specifications are not visible or readable in any photo.
Current stock or readiness for sale cannot be confirmed from photos alone.

risks.risk: Machine may not function or may have internal mechanical or electrical damage.
risks.proof: Video of the machine running with waste nylon fed into the hopper and raw material output.

risks.risk: Machine may be used or refurbished rather than brand new.
risks.proof: Purchase invoice or close-up photos showing unused condition, intact seals, and original packaging.

risks.risk: Machine may be missing dies, screens, heaters, control panel, or other components.
risks.proof: Detailed photos of the die head, cutter, electrical panel, and all accessories.

risks.risk: Electrical supply may not match Nigerian voltage, phase, or frequency.
risks.proof: Photo of the motor or data plate showing voltage, phase, and frequency ratings.

risks.risk: Machine may not be suitable for nylon specifically; different plastics require different screw and barrel configurations.
risks.proof: Manufacturer specifications or video showing nylon processing output.
risks.if_unproven: as general plastic extruder, not confirmed for nylon

proof_requests: Video of the machine operating with waste nylon input and raw material output.
Close-up photo of any nameplate, motor label, or control panel showing voltage, power, and brand.
Photos showing the die head, cutter, and pelletizing system.
Invoice or documentation supporting the "brand new" claim.
response.reason: The item is identifiable by type as a nylon/plastic recycling extruder, and it can be priced at its worst case (non-working, unverified condition) while listing the proof needed to raise the value.
